headline: Moonbow Viewing and Lodge Reservations
reservation: Entry to the state park is generally open, but the historic DuPont Lodge and riverside campsites require advance booking, especially during the 5-day moonbow window. Official moonbow dates are published annually; verify these and specific viewing area access with Kentucky State Parks.

days.title: The Niagara of the South

stops.name: Main Falls Overlook
stops.detail: Witness the 68-foot drop and the intense mist that characterizes this massive sandstone shelf.

stops.name: Cumberland Falls Visitor Center
stops.detail: Review the geology of the Appalachian Plateau and the history of the moonbow phenomenon.

days.driving: Walking within park core; conditions vary
days.note: Mist can make paved observation decks slippery; wear footwear with grip.

days.title: Rugged River Cliffs

stops.name: Eagle Falls Trail
stops.detail: A moderately strenuous hike rewarding visitors with a side-profile view of the main falls across the river.

stops.name: Moonbow Trail
stops.detail: Follow the cliffline through hemlock groves to see dramatic rock formations along the Cumberland River.

days.driving: Minimal driving between park trailheads; conditions vary
days.note: High river levels can submerge lower trail sections; check daily safety alerts.

days.title: Corbin History and Forest Lakes

stops.name: Harland Sanders Cafe and Museum
stops.detail: Explore the culinary history of the region at the original site of Kentucky Fried Chicken.

stops.name: Laurel River Lake
stops.detail: A quiet contrast to the falls, offering clear blue waters for swimming or lakeside picnics.

days.driving: Allow 1.5 hours for regional transit; conditions vary
days.note: Watch for deer and local wildlife on winding two-lane roads at dusk.

intel.title: Moonbow Night Congestion
intel.text: Parking lots at the main falls frequently reach capacity during the full moon cycle. Arrive early in the afternoon to secure a spot for nighttime viewing.

intel.title: Daniel Boone National Forest Gaps
intel.text: Cellular reception is extremely limited within the gorge and surrounding forest. Download regional maps before departing Corbin or London.

intel.title: Gateway Service Hubs
intel.text: Fuel up in Corbin or Williamsburg as there are no service stations within the park boundaries. Carry basic supplies for long hikes on the Moonbow Trail.

intel.title: Spring Flow vs. Summer Clarity
intel.text: Spring rains (April-June) provide maximum volume, while late summer offers clearer, turquoise water. Visit mid-week to avoid heavy regional weekend crowds.

intel.title: Flood Risk and Deck Closures
intel.text: Heavy rains can cause the Cumberland River to rise rapidly, closing lower observation platforms. Check the official park social media for real-time safety closures.

plan.arrival: Fly into TYS (Knoxville), rent a vehicle, and drive two hours north via I-75 to Corbin for supplies before park entry.
plan.vehicle: Standard passenger cars are sufficient for main park roads; no special off-road vehicle is required for primary overlooks.
plan.goldenHour: The Gatliff Bridge offers a framed view of the river gorge during late afternoon, depending on leaf cover.
